title: Nucleus POC bench stitchup review
summary: Quick weekly POC sync to compare Redwood bench numbers vs customer incumbent. Nucleus cares most about p95 latency under 280ms for 512-token prompts and maintaining cost per 1k requests below their current vendor. We reviewed delta table, identified two hotspots (KV cache miss rate + batch sizing), and agreed next steps: share updated bench sheet, provision a 2-hour dedicated slot for head-to-head, SE deep-dive on quant profiles, and legal to review SOC2 appendix.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Tom (Redwood AE), Liya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Marcus (CTO, Nucleus), Rachel (ML Eng), Dev (SRE), Ana (Product)

Summary: quick bench readout, two main deltas vs incumbent, agree next steps for dedicated slot and quant tuning

[00:00] Tom: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Marcus: yep loud and clear, thanks Tom. we had a quick sync internally and wanted to see the raw numbers from last week's lab runs.
[00:10] Tom: perfect. Liya will run through the table, i'll call out the major deltas vs your incumbent baseline. liya over to you.
[00:16] Liya: cool thanks. so in the sheet we ran three mixes: short prompts ~64 tokens, mid 256, and long 512. the p50/p95 numbers are here, note that for 512 tokens we see p95 at around 310ms on our default hosted profile while your baseline reported 270ms in their run.
[00:34] Rachel: wait 310? we were expecting closer to 280 from your earlier notes. is that with quant or without?
[00:40] Liya: that's with 8-bit quant enabled but default batch sizing. i should mention our run had a KV cache cold-start for about 8% of requests which pushed the p95 up. when we forced a warmed-kv run the p95 dropped to 280–290ms.
[00:58] Dev: can you explain what you mean by KV cache cold start? our current vendor had a persistent local cache, i'm worried if your cache warms slower it could affect production tail.
[01:06] Liya: yeah totally — at high level Redwood uses prefix/KV caching across GPU shards; on a fresh sequence the KV entries need to be repopulated which adds ~20–40ms for that request. our autoscaler and routing usually keep a high cache hit for sustained traffic, but in bursty patterns you'll see more cold misses.
[01:25] Marcus: and that 20–40ms is per-token or once per request?
[01:29] Liya: it's roughly once per request slice — the initial KV refilling cost, so it's not per-token but it affects the latency of the early tokens which shows up in p95.
[01:36] Rachel: ok that explains part of it. second question — what about batching? our baseline seems to trade higher latency for much lower unit cost by batching aggressively during peaks. are you comparing apples to apples on batch sizes?
[01:47] Tom: good call. the benchmark we sent used conservative batch target to meet a tighter latency SLO. we can re-run a throughput-optimized profile to show the cost delta at higher batch sizes.
[01:58] Dev: what were the batch sizes you used in the mid/512 run?
[02:01] Liya: default target batch was 8 for 512 token sequences; incumbent runs used batch 16–24 in their peak runs. that's why their per-request CPU/GPU utilization looked more efficient.
[02:12] Marcus: so basically you're faster on warm cache but they squeeze more throughput when they accept higher tail — that's the tradeoff we thought.
[02:18] Liya: yep exactly. we also saw better token-efficiency once we adjusted quant profile — the 4-bit-like quant we used in some runs shaved ~12% unit cost but increased p95 by 30–40ms, so it's a trade.
[02:31] Rachel: does that 4-bit quant mean int4 or some mixed-precision trick? our models are slightly sensitive, we had output quality drifts with aggressive quant at PAUSE.
[02:39] Liya: it's a mixed q4_0 path — not pure int4, more like hybrid block quant. quality delta in our evals was minimal on your prompt set but we'll share the eval diffs. there are a few anchor prompts where the probabilities shift and results need manual review.
[02:55] Ana: is that the eval run you ran on the five canonical prompts we shared?
[02:58] Liya: yes, the sample set you provided plus a random 500 sample from your logs. overall bleu/rouge-ish metrics had sub-2% drift on the primary prompts.
[03:07] Marcus: ok good. back to the p95 delta — you mentioned a warmed run got you to ~285. can we replicate the incumbent's 270 without sacrificing cost?
[03:16] Tom: short answer: probably not at exactly 270 with the same cost, but we can get close with a combination of dedicated slot routing (to avoid cold KV), slightly larger batch target, and a tuned quant profile. we'll run a head-to-head dedicated slot so your team sees identical warm/cache conditions.
[03:31] Dev: what's a dedicated slot mean in this context? isolated GPU pool?
[03:34] Liya: it's a reserved capacity nodepool for your tenant — no noisy neighbors, warmed caches, pinned model variant. latency variance tends to narrow in that mode. we can provision a 2-hour window for the test.
[03:44] Marcus: cost for that test window?
[03:46] Tom: we'll cover the short dedicated run for free during the POC — no charge. if you want ongoing reserved capacity that's a different contract.
[03:52] Rachel: nice. can we instrument more metrics — specifically per-request KV hit/miss, batch sizes, GPU occupancy, and a breakdown of kernel times?
[04:02] Liya: yes, we'll output a detailed CSV with those fields. note kernel times may include some proprietary naming — sometimes the trace labels (like kernel_12_b1) are opaque, we'll map them to higher-level phases.
[04:13] Marcus: competitor question: your incumbent uses a different runtime that does some fused attention kernels that they call "fast-attn". can Redwood match that?
[04:22] Liya: our compilation selects optimized kernels per architecture; in some cases we already have a fused attention that performs similarly. but differences show up at long sequences. we'll surface the kernel select logs so you can compare.
[04:33] Dev: regarding security — we need SOC2 type II and a KMS/HSM integration. where are you on that?
[04:39] Tom: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, support for BYOK via KMS integrations, and an HSM option in private deployments. we'll drop the compliance appendix into the workspace.
[04:48] Marcus: make sure to include retention policy details — our legal team needs a full audit trail if we go live.
[04:52] Samir: noted, i'll attach the retention and audit logs doc after the call.
[04:56] Rachel: back to tuning — Liya can you outline the tuning plan in three bullets?
[05:00] Liya: sure — 1) warm the KV via a synthetic pre-warm pass and run a 2-hour steady state at target qps; 2) run a throughput profile with batch targets 16 and 24 to show cost per 1k requests; 3) run a quality check on the quant profiles (q8/q4 hybrid) against your prompt set and send eval diffs.
[05:18] Marcus: that sounds reasonable. what's your expected delta on unit cost if we move from batch 8->16 with q8?
[05:23] Liya: ballpark 18–25% lower unit cost on GPU cycles for sustained traffic. we'll quantify in the spreadsheet.
[05:29] Ana: i also want a simple table that maps "what we lose" vs "what we gain" for latency vs cost per profile so product can decide.
[05:36] Tom: we'll include that decision matrix.
[05:38] Dev: one more operational question — if we see performance regressions in canary, do you support automatic fallback to the incumbent or a smaller model?
[05:46] Liya: yes, Redwood supports routing policies with automatic fallback to pinned variants or to a secondary region/model. for POC we'll show an example canary policy.
[05:54] Rachel: excellent. for the dedicated slot run, can we capture both raw traces and decoded outputs so our QA can validate semantics?
[05:59] Liya: yes, we can include trace + decoded outputs. we'll redaction-mask PII per your compliance settings.
[06:07] Marcus: logistics — propose we do the dedicated head-to-head Wednesday morning (2026-07-06) 14:00 UTC for 2 hours.
[06:13] Tom: works for us, i'll schedule and provision.
[06:16] Samir: i'll send calendar invite and workspace link with the spreadsheet.
[06:19] Ana: last ask — can you include an explicit column with "KV hit rate" in the summary so it's not hidden?
[06:24] Liya: yes will do.
[06:26] Tom: ok quick recap of action items then: tom will send bench sheet, liya runs dedicated slot and tuning runs, marcus provides incumbent traces, dev grants staging log access. any other asks?
[06:36] Marcus: none from me. thanks.
[06:38] Tom: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the invite and docs.
[06:41] End of call
notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'KV cash' or 'quantize' instead of exact kernel names) — confirmed by SE. Customer prioritized p95 latency and cost per 1k requests; agreed on dedicated slot test 2026-07-06 14:00 UTC; Redwood to send detailed bench CSV and eval diffs.
